slides.title: Fold Expressions Overview
slides.prompt: C++17 Fold Expressions provide concise syntax to apply binary operators across parameter packs without writing recursive template boilerplate.

slides.title: Unary Right Fold Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator structure for a unary right fold (args op ...).

slides.title: Types of Fold Expressions
slides.prompt: How many forms of fold expressions exist in C++17?
options: 4 forms (Unary Left, Unary Right, Binary Left, Binary Right)
2 forms (Left fold and Right fold only)
slides.correctAnswer: 4 forms (Unary Left, Unary Right, Binary Left, Binary Right)

slides.title: Binary Left Fold with Initial Value
slides.prompt: Fill in the initial value part of a binary left fold (init + ... + args).

slides.title: Unary Fold on Empty Packs
slides.prompt: Which binary operators are allowed in a unary fold over an empty parameter pack?
options: No operators are allowed; empty packs always cause compile errors in unary folds

slides.title: Fold Expression with Comma Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the fold operator used to execute a function call on every argument in a pack.

slides.title: Unary Left vs Unary Right Evaluation Order
slides.prompt: For inputs (1, 2, 3), how does unary left fold (... + args) expand compared to unary right fold (args + ...)?
options: Both expand identically as (1 + 2 + 3) without parenthesis evaluation differences
Unary Left evaluates right to left

slides.title: Logical AND Fold Expression
slides.prompt: Fill in the logical operator used to verify all boolean conditions in a parameter pack are true.

slides.title: Parentheses Requirement in Fold Expressions
slides.prompt: Are surrounding parentheses mandatory when writing C++17 fold expressions?
options: Yes, fold expressions must always be enclosed in parentheses e.g. (... + args)
No, parentheses are optional unless disambiguating precedence
Only when using binary left folds
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, fold expressions must always be enclosed in parentheses e.g. (... + args)

slides.title: Push Back Fold Example
slides.prompt: Fill in the method name in a comma fold to append all arguments into a std::vector.
